summary: Build practical crisis and disaster journalism skills in verification, safety, interviewing, and newsroom planning. Enrol in the five-day course.
lede: Crisis and disaster journalism training helps reporters, editors, producers, and communication officers make coverage decisions during emergencies. It focuses on accurate public-interest reporting when information is incomplete and access or resources are constrained. Participants practise triangulating sources, checking images and locations, assessing field risks, conducting consent-based interviews, and managing corrections.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who make, commission, verify, publish, or support media coverage during crisis and disaster journalism assignments.
prerequisites: You should have working experience in journalism, media production, newsroom coordination, humanitarian communication, or a related communications role. Familiarity with digital publishing and basic source verification will help, but coding is not required. You should bring a laptop for browser-based verification exercises. Advanced OSINT automation and technical digital forensics are introduced at conceptual and operational levels rather than the implementation level.
